summary: This bill amends the Clean Air Act to bar nonattainment designations for areas that would meet ozone or particulate-matter standards but for emissions from outside the United States (regardless of human origin) and to exempt Severe/Extreme ozone or Serious PM areas from sanctions and fees when they demonstrate that foreign emissions, exceptional events, or uncontrollable mobile sources caused the shortfall, while requiring renewed demonstrations every five years.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Clean Air Act regarding nonattainment designations and sanctions but contains no provisions that authorize, increase, decrease, or otherwise affect federal appropriations or government spending levels.
No provisions in the bill address tax rates, tax policy, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
The legislation deals exclusively with air quality standards under the Clean Air Act and has no connection to healthcare delivery, insurance, or public health coverage systems.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues appear in the bill.

While the bill references emissions 'emanating from outside of the United States,' this is strictly an environmental/air-quality provision and does not alter immigration law, border policy, or pathways for legal immigration.
The bill contains no language related to reproductive rights, abortion access, or related healthcare regulations.
No provisions affect military budgets, defense spending, or national security appropriations.

The bill directly amends the Clean Air Act (Sections 179B and new 179C) to prevent nonattainment designations and waive sanctions/fees when areas fail to meet ozone or particulate-matter standards solely because of foreign emissions (including non-anthropogenic sources), exceptional events, or uncontrollable mobile-source emissions. This explicitly limits the reach and enforcement of federal air-quality regulations.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, food assistance, unemployment benefits, or other safety-net entitlements.
The bill has no bearing on schools, federal education funding, school choice, or education policy.
No references to controlled substances, drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related criminal penalties.
The legislation does not address sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal-justice reform.
Although foreign emissions are mentioned, the bill does not establish tariffs, trade agreements, import restrictions, or other trade-policy measures; the focus remains environmental compliance.
No fiscal provisions, deficit targets, or debt-related measures are present.
The bill contains no language concerning LGBTQ+ legal protections or anti-discrimination rules.
No provisions address foreign assistance, international aid programs, or related funding.
No election-administration, voting-access, or campaign-finance provisions exist.
The bill does not regulate technology companies, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions affect collective bargaining, union rights, or labor standards.
The legislation does not address religious exemptions, civil-rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and anti-discrimination rules.
